thread:
marco-se: pinging the thread — AtlasWave POC seeing really slow TTFT in morning tests, some first tokens ~3s. They're on rwd-open-13b-q4, 16k context, default batching. Can we triage?

atlaswave-admin: confirmed. Repro script attached in case notes. No infra changes on our side. We're running 15 parallel workers hitting route `atlaswave-prod` for preflight.

infra-bot: runtime log snippet: `WARN dispatch.go:140 avg_dispatch_ms=480 batch_fill_ms=220 batch_size_avg=1.2 kv_cache_hit=0.12`

anya-eng: Yikes, avg_dispatch_ms ~480 + tiny batch_size = head-of-line. Looks like client is sending many small requests and the dispatcher is waiting to fill. Any route hints configured?

marco-se: They didn't set any prefill or warmup. SDK call is just `_client.generate({model: "rwd-open-13b-q4", prompt, max_tokens: 256})`.

lucy-support: Billing question from procurement: if we enable warm prefill will that be charged? Also they asked about Dedicated vs Hosted for bursty patterns.

anya-eng: Short answers: yes, prefill/warmup consumes tokens and will be billed on Hosted. Dedicated with reserved capacity avoids route_concurrency limits and is cheaper under high sustained QPS.

deployer: Found entries at 09:10 UTC: `ERROR rate_limiter.go:101: token_bucket_empty route=atlaswave-prod` and `ERR shard_queue.go:78: shard_queue_timeout wait_ms=600`.

marco-se: So that explains intermittent 429s + slow TTFT. If rate limiter blocks, retries queue and batch windows grow.

anya-eng: Immediate mitigations: (1) set `prefill_policy: "warm_local"` on their route for KV warming for top prompts (2) reduce `batch_window_ms` from default to 50ms or set `latency_slo_ms: 180` so runtime prefers lower-latency dispatch, (3) add `burst_capacity: 30` for short bursts if on Dedicated or increase concurrency_limit for hosted trial.

atlaswave-admin: Did the team try warm_local? Concerned about token billing and security since some prompts include PII.

lucy-support: For security: on Private (VPC) deployment, prefill/warmup runs inside customer infra and KMS never leaves their control. On Hosted, we have KMS integrations but plaintext traverses our managed runtime briefly — legal noted that. We'll include templated answer for the security questionnaire.

anya-eng: Quick test — I pushed `latency_slo_ms:180` to a canary route and enabled `prefill_policy: "warm_local"` for top-10 prompts. Results: single-turn TTFT median down from 900ms -> 360ms, and kv_cache_hit up to 0.68 in 2m. Still seeing spikes at very high concurrency.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled +1 p4d at 09:12 UTC. But logs show burst > concurrency_limit triggered until scale completed.

marco-se: Customer also runs a 20-parallel stress test which still causes occasional 429. They want guidance to be able to do sustained 20qps in production.

anya-eng: For sustained 20 qps we recommend (A) Dedicated reserved pool with burst_capacity, (B) client-side pacing + exponential backoff + jitter, (C) pre-warming with scheduled warmup jobs before peak windows.

lucy-support: I'll draft a presales note that explains token cost for warmup (estimate: ~0.5-1% of daily usage depending on prompt lengths) and include Dedicated commit tiers with ballpark pricing.

deployer: Helpful debug commands: `grep -E "token_bucket_empty|shard_queue_timeout|avg_dispatch_ms" /var/log/runtime/*.log` and metrics endpoint: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/route-metrics?route=atlaswave-prod" | jq`

atlaswave-admin: We'll try the canary config. Also legal asked: can warmup be scoped to non-sensitive prompts only?

anya-eng: Yes — prefill_policy can accept a matched prompt set or tag. We can scope KV prefetch to hashed prompt IDs so you only warm non-PII prompts.

marco-se: Can we get eng on a quick call at 13:30 UTC to review Dedicated vs host tweaks and ramp plan? They're ready to decide after meeting.

anya-eng: I can make 13:30. I'll bring a short runbook and perf graphs. Please collect a 5-10 prompt corpus and your exact concurrency script so we can repro.

lucy-support: I'll prepare the security questionnaire snippet and cost ballpark.

atlaswave-admin: Thanks all, sending prompt set + stress script now. We'll expect the 13:30 invite.

marco-se: Closing notes: action items -> eng will share runbook and canary config, support will send pricing/security bullets, sales will host meeting. Follow-up thread after call for final config. :thumbsup:
